note: Frozen mtime-derived git provenance. mtime does not survive copying; this file does. The rewrite reads this instead of the reflog, which also makes it reproducible.

caveat.summary: collection_code_digest d4a5f4a401dc9c3f names the code at the recorded commits, which is NOT the code that ran, for all 304 episodes. git_commit and git_tree are correct; only the digest's claim about execution is false.
caveat.cause: The working tree was AHEAD of HEAD. The joint-state logging that this collection exists to produce was uncommitted while it ran, and was committed as 1d652ae after the last episode finished. code_digest() reads `git show <commit>:<file>`, so it describes the commit and structurally cannot see uncommitted work.
proofs: FIELD IN THE DATA, ABSENT FROM THE CODE: every episode carries 24 joint_*_pos_rad / joint_*_vel_radps columns. dataset.py at both recorded commits (32e1a483, 094f4a06) contains zero occurrences of JOINT_STATE_FIELDS; 1d652ae contains three.
TIMESTAMPS: last episode written 12:08:15, commit 1d652ae at 12:08:58 -- 43 seconds after the collection ended.
caveat.data_impact: None. The executing code is exactly 1d652ae's, which is committed and diffable. The direction is favourable: the data is RICHER than its recorded commits, carrying columns they could not have written.
caveat.note: Same defect sbel-pc found on their rigid half, same direction (tree ahead of HEAD), hit here within an hour of writing it up as a lesson -- which is the argument for the durable fix (record the running process's state) rather than for being more careful.
